title: Local effacement of positive derived-function rows for the procyclic norm-scalar bar
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $A(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ with all continuous maps on the small coherent profinite site, in common coefficient universes [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Put $H=\mathbf Z_\ell$ with its additive inverse-limit topology [def-sfb-ind-unipotent-system]. Give the regular internal $A$-module the trivial $H$-action [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Fix any nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $A[0]\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and a compatible bar model of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. Let $U$ forget the action. For each open subgroup $J\subseteq H$, including $H$, form
$$D_J^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline J^p],UI^q)\quad(p,q\geq0),$$
zero otherwise, with the action-dependent inhomogeneous bar differential $d_h$ and commuting resolution differential $d_v$ [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sp-double-complex-total]. Define internal module sheaves
$$V_{J,q}^p=H^q(D_J^{p,\bullet},d_v),\qquad V_{J,q}^{-1}=0,$$
where kernels and images are taken in the sheaf category before section evaluation [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The induced horizontal differential is also denoted $d_h$. Restriction along $K^p\hookrightarrow J^p$ for an open subgroup $K\subseteq J$ induces $r_{J,K}:V_{J,q}^\bullet\to V_{K,q}^\bullet$.

For every open $J\subseteq H$, profinite test space $S$, $q\geq1$, $p\geq0$, and section $x\in V_{J,q}^p(S)$ satisfying $d_hx=0$, there are a finite jointly surjective family $\{u_i:S_i\to S\}$, open subgroups $K_i\subseteq J$, and sections $y_i\in V_{K_i,q}^{p-1}(S_i)$ such that
$$r_{J,K_i}(u_i^*x)=d_hy_i.$$
For $p=0$ this says the restricted section is zero. The assertion concerns every compatible model and every such injective resolution. Empty test spaces are included. This is local effacement after shrinking the procyclic group; it imposes no global positive Cech exactness and no vanishing of the individual positive vertical cohomology sheaves. The field $\Omega$ remains noncomplete and all continuous functions are retained.
